panels.description: Total GPU kernel launches in the selected time range. A quick sanity check of how busy the GPU has been.
panels.title: Total CUDA Kernel Launches

panels.description: Total failed CUDA calls (non-zero return code). Drill into Panel 9 to see which function and error code.
panels.title: Total CUDA errors

panels.description: Total times HAMi rejected an allocation because the workload exceeded its memory quota. A strong sign that memory needs more headroom.
panels.title: Total HAMi OOM Errors

panels.description: Kernels submitted to the GPU per second, per pod. A sudden drop while the pod is still Running usually means a stall — check the Errors row or memory.
panels.title: CUDA Kernel Launch Rate

panels.description: How often the workload replays a CUDA Graph. Non-zero values mean the framework is using graph optimisation (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, torch.cuda.graphs).
panels.title: CUDA Graph Launch Rate

panels.description: How long the CPU thread waited just to submit a kernel (not GPU runtime). Spikes mean a full GPU queue or HAMi throttling — see Panel 20.
panels.title: Host-Side CUDA Kernel Launch Latency P95/P99

panels.description: Bytes/second successfully allocated on the GPU. Steady growth without matching frees indicates a memory leak.
panels.title: GPU Memory Allocation Rate

panels.description: Allocation calls per second. Many small alloc calls in a row indicates fragmentation risk.
panels.title: GPU Memory Allocation Call Rate

panels.description: Average bytes per allocation. Very small averages suggest the workload isn't using a caching allocator.
panels.title: Average Memory Allocation Size

panels.description: Data movement per second, by direction. Host→Device dominates during data loading; Device→Device dominates during NCCL all-reduce in multi-GPU training.
panels.title: Memory Copy Traffic by Direction

panels.description: Bytes/second of GPU memory freed. Pair with Allocation Rate: a persistent gap (alloc > free) indicates a leak.
panels.title: GPU Memory Free Rate

panels.description: Free calls per second. Pair with Allocation Call Rate: large persistent imbalance indicates a leak or over-eager release.
panels.title: GPU Memory Free Call Rate

panels.description: Bytes/second of GPU memory zero/fill (memset). High rates often mean wasteful buffer re-init that could be replaced with reuse.
panels.title: Memset Traffic — Sync vs Async (bytes/s)

panels.description: Direct GPU↔GPU transfer bytes/second (via NVLink). Non-zero only for multi-GPU workloads.
panels.title: P2P Peer Copy Traffic (bytes/s)

panels.description: New CUDA errors per interval, broken down by function and error code. Common codes: 2 = OOM, 1 = invalid argument, 400 = bad handle.
panels.title: CUDA Errors per Interval

panels.description: New HAMi quota-denied allocations per interval, by function and memory kind. Non-zero = increase the ResourceClaim memory limit.
panels.title: HAMi OOM Events per Interval

panels.description: All HAMi OOM tuples in the selected time range, even for pods that have already exited. Sort to see which functions fail most.
panels.title: HAMi OOM Events Over Time

panels.description: How long HAMi's rate limiter delayed each kernel launch. Persistently high values mean the SM quota is too tight.
panels.title: HAMi throttle P95/P99

panels.description: Host-thread wait time in cuStreamSynchronize — how long the CPU blocked for a specific stream to drain. High values indicate GPU backpressure on that stream.
panels.title: CUDA Stream Sync Latency P95/P99

panels.description: Host-thread wait time in cuCtxSynchronize / cuDeviceSynchronize — full-device barrier. Sustained high P99 is a strong backpressure signal (see Phase 4 device_sync_p99).
panels.title: CUDA Device Sync Latency P95/P99

panels.description: Host-thread wait time in cuEventSynchronize — how long the CPU blocked waiting on a recorded CUDA event.
panels.title: CUDA Event Sync Latency P95/P99

panels.description: Distribution of grid size (gridX*gridY*gridZ = total CUDA blocks) per kernel launch. P95/P99 reveal the largest kernels scheduled. Source: gpu_cuda_kernel_grid_size_total (Prometheus histogram).
panels.title: Kernel Grid Size P95/P99 (blocks/launch)

panels.description: Distribution of block size (blockX*blockY*blockZ = threads per block) per kernel launch. Source: gpu_cuda_kernel_block_size_total (Prometheus histogram).
panels.title: Kernel Block Size P95/P99 (threads/launch)
